content.text:
**Here are the 5 most notable recent tweets** (from the last few days, primarily Aug 7–10, 2026) on AI-generated spam/slop flooding bug bounty programs, including specific cases like Apple, Microsoft payouts, payout adjustments, and AI-assisted triage/evaluation:

- **@0xConda** (Brandon Rossi): “AI may kill bug bounty. Bug bounty has historically attracted some of the ‘get rich quick’ crowd. With AI lowering the barrier of entry to essentially zero, people without the skill and knowledge to validate their own reports are submitting tons of AI slop to programs.” (High-engagement thread starter on how spam devalues real research; 142 likes).[[1]](https://x.com/0xConda/status/2086483094970736805)

- **@NitinGavhane_**: “AI is taking over bug hunting in 2026. Microsoft just dropped a record $20M+ in bounties, AI found a 15-year-old Linux root bug + ancient Chrome flaws, while platforms fight ‘AI slop’ reports & cut payouts. Wild times for hunters!” (Directly ties Microsoft record payouts, AI discoveries, slop fights, and payout cuts).[[2]](https://x.com/NitinGavhane_/status/2086680535582077400)

- **@ChrisShort**: “Imagine how open source maintainers feel | Apple's bug bounty program is drowning in so much AI slop, it is in danger of missing serious exploits” (with Bitdefender link; echoes the exact “Apple missing real exploit due to AI noise” concern).[[3]](https://x.com/ChrisShort/status/2086846218198487156)

- **@jeetbhdr** (Siddharth): “In the name of AI slop valid reports of researchers gets marked as N/A they need to go out of the way to get the bounty. Find bugs fight for bounty whats next?” (Highlights how AI noise leads to valid submissions being dismissed or requiring extra effort).[[4]](https://x.com/jeetbhdr/status/2086697522857480270)

- **@RexNetpl** (RexNet Mateusz Mieczkowski): “AI is definitely disrupting bug bounty right now, mainly by creating more noise and longer triage queues. … Programs will adapt with better filtering, validation requirements, reputation systems, and AI-assisted triage of their own.” (Discusses AI noise impact and emerging AI-judged evaluation/triage solutions).[[5]](https://x.com/RexNetpl/status/2086531049417224386)

These capture the core discussion on spam flooding (especially Apple), payout shifts (Microsoft records + cuts), and AI’s dual role in both generating noise and aiding triage. Other posts echo the same themes but with lower visibility or less specificity.
